abstract: Micro-dramas (duanju) are reshaping digital production and consumption, yet a lack of longitudinal data connecting series to their platform visibility persists, limiting our understanding of the emerging medium. We introduce HongguoTrending, a longitudinal, multimodal dataset of hourly snapshots from seven trending lists of Hongguo, China's largest micro-drama platform. Collected through a two-stage asynchronous pipeline, the archive links 63,200 ranking entries across 632 web list-hours and 157 client hours (889 distinct series) to metadata, cover images, sampled episode videos, and audience engagement metrics. Exploratory analyses show distinct turnover rates between web and mobile trending lists, production-driven mainstream values alongside kinship-centered synopses, genre-specific cover palettes, and strong associations between user sharing and next-day rank gains. Accessible via a RESTful API, this dataset supports empirical research on algorithmic gatekeeping, popularity dynamics, and multimodal digital culture.

title: HongguoTrending: A Longitudinal, Multimodal Archive of Trending Videos and Topics on a Leading Micro-Drama Platform
